dream: The turnip slid off the fence and rolled into a corner that was not there. It bumped the tall fence, which bent like a tired knee. The card hummed a low, wet sound that felt like rain hitting a roof I could not touch. I pressed my tired wedge down to catch the air, but the air felt like thick paper, heavy and damp. The fence leaned harder, trying to bite the turnip, while the wedge slid again, unsure if it was real or just a drawing of weight. I woke the wedge up by pressing harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the cool hum faded into a dream of a flat, heavy stone waiting to slip.
